the ionized gas in these galaxies has characteristics indicative of outflowing winds, and the most IR-lumious galaxy shows strong evidence of outflowing gas.
we detect ionized gas outflowing from the disks of galaxies in an assembling galaxy group, but we cannot rule out that some or all of the emission is from gas in the disk.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find ionized gas outflows and extraplanary gas in a significant fraction of the most luminous galaxies in a supergroup at z = 37 that will eventually form a Coma-like cluster.
we have detected ionized gas outflows in 3 of 18 disk-dominated galaxies in the central supergroup of the z = 0 supergroup that will merge to create the Coma Cluster.
we detect outflows in ~18% of IR luminous, disk-dominated, galaxies in a galaxy group in the process of merging to form a Comamass cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supergroup members with the highest SFRs have the strongest outflow signatures, which is consistent with a picture in which the winds are driven by star formation.
winds are common in star-forming galaxies at z = 1, but are not ubiquitous in galaxies in a cluster-forming super-group at z ~ 0.3.
the most IR luminous galaxies are driving winds in a manner similar to local ULIRGs.
